Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of South Africa Women. The artificial lights are already on as things have gotten a bit dark in Benoni, but there doesn't seem to be any rain on the horizon. Anushka Sharma and Shafali Verma are all set to open the innings for India Women. Eliz-Mari Marx will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Spinners pull India back before late damage - India Women failed to find an early breakthrough, but the spinners brought them right back into the game during the middle overs, keeping the runs in check while also picking up key wickets. Sree Charani was the standout in that phase with 2/22, while Deepti Sharma also chipped in with a couple, though she was taken apart in the final over. Renuka Singh was the pick of the bowlers with 2/21, and overall, the bowling unit has done its job. It now comes down to the batters, who will be chasing for the first time in the series and will need a strong performance to finish on a high. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

From control to collapse to a strong finish - South Africa Women once again started well, racking up 49 runs in the Powerplay. Sune Luus struggled to get going, but Laura Wolvaardt looked fluent and in complete control yet again. The pair added 75 runs before a sudden collapse saw them slip from 75/1 to 124/6. However, the skipper held one end firmly and kept the scoreboard moving. Sinalo Jafta then came in and played a few lusty blows, while Wolvaardt remained unbeaten on 92 off 56, as they smashed 29 runs in the final two overs to push the total past the 150-run mark.

Game in the balance - A good battle between bat and ball on a surface that's on the slower side and offering some assistance to the spinners. South Africa Women have posted a competitive total, but considering the start they had, they would have hoped for more. India Women pulled things back beautifully through the middle overs, conceding just 28 runs between overs 10 to 15, showing great control and discipline. However, Deepti Sharma did concede 16 runs in the final over, which has shifted the momentum slightly back in South Africa's favour and added a late twist to this contest.

Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we are all set for the action to begin. The two teams stride out in the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be India's first, followed by the national anthem of South Africa. We are now done with the pre-match formalities. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. South Africa Women take their respective field positions. Laura Wolvaardt and Sune Luus open up for the South Africa Women. Kranti Gaud has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Victor Mpitsang and Nono Pongolo are pitchside. They say that the pitch had hard-rolled grass, making it fast, bouncy, and excellent for batting without offering much movement to the bowlers. They say that the ground is known for high scores and has large side boundaries. Because it is hard to guess a safe total to defend, Pongolo believed the winning captain would choose to bowl first. Mpitsang agreed that chasing a target would be the best plan for the game.

Shafali Verma is in for a chat - Shafali Verma says that they have had a good partnership in the last game, did well with the ball, which gave them confidence, and they are ready to win this game. Adds that she was trying to get more runs in the Powerplay by hitting it over the circle. Shafali shares that the journey has been with a lot of ups and downs but she is trying to give her best. Ends by saying that they have lost the series, but they will try and win this game and finish on a positive note.

A quick chat with Eliz-Mari Marx - Eliz-Mari Marx says that she is privileged to be back in the side and tries to bring positivity to the team. Adds that going back home and reassessing her bowling plans helped her a lot and it came off well in the last game. Feels that she wants to be consistent and impact the game. On her ball-striking ability, she says that she's put a lot of effort into the mental side of the game, which has then helped the physical side of her game as well.

With South Africa celebrating Freedom Day, marking the nation’s first democratic elections in 1994, the final game carries added significance, blending cricket with a day of unity and history, making the occasion even more special.

South Africa Women (Playing XI) - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Sune Luus, Tazmin Brits, Annerie Dercksen, Anneke Bosch (In for Tumi Sekhukhune), Chloe Tryon, Nadine De Klerk (In for Kayla Reyneke), Sinalo Jafta (WK), Eliz-Mari Marx, Ayabonga Khaka, Nonkululeko Mlaba.

India Women (Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Anushka Sharma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh (WK), Arundhati Reddy (In for Kashvee Gautam), Kranti Gaud, Sree Charani, Renuka Singh Thakur.

The skipper of India Women - Harmanpreet Kaur says that they wanted to bowl first, and it's good they got the opportunity to do that today. Adds that the last game was a good one for them and they executed their plans well and will look to have the same clarity today as well. On any changes in the team, Kaur says that the likes of Smriti and Kashvee are resting, and Arundhati Reddy is back in the team.

The skipper of South Africa Women - Laura Wolvaardt says that it doesn't happen often that she has won five tosses in a row. Adds that they have been bowling first all series, so wants to see how they do batting first here. Mentions that the wicket tends to be on the slower side and it was a quick turnaround, they have assessed the conditions quickly. Laura says that she is happy with how they have bounced back from a disappointing New Zealand series. Informs that they have made a couple of changes with Anneke Bosch and Nadine De Klerk coming back in the side. Ends by saying that they want to finish the series on a high note.
TOSS - Both skippers have made their way out in the middle. 'Heads' is the call by Harmanpreet Kaur, and it lands as 'Tails'. Laura informs that South Africa Women will be BATTING FIRST.

The final showdown - The stage is set for a cracking finale. Can the unstoppable Laura Wolvaardt, who leads the series charts by a mile with 238 runs, and top wicket-taker Tumi Sekhukhune put the finishing touches on a dominant home campaign? Or will India defy the odds, brush aside their mounting injury list, and sign off from South Africa with back-to-back victories? Grab the edge of your seats as the live action is just moments away. Toss and team news in a bit...

The pace crisis - The momentum might be shifting, but the visitors are stepping onto the field today with a severely depleted pace arsenal. The injury ward is unfortunately overflowing. Amanjot Kaur is out with an injury, Arundhati Reddy is battling as well, and losing Kranti Gaud to a fielding injury last game was a massive blow. With the Benoni track historically promising some bounce, India's makeshift bowling attack will be put to the ultimate test this afternoon.

India's roaring comeback - After a harsh reality check in the first three matches where they failed to defend their totals, highlighted by that record-breaking 183-run opening stand and blistering century from skipper Laura Wolvaardt, the Women in Blue finally found their bite in game four. It was an absolute masterclass from Deepti Sharma. Her swashbuckling late-order hitting alongside Richa Ghosh pushed India to a formidable 185, before Deepti spun a web around the South African batters to claim a career-best 5/19 and secure a thrilling 14-run victory.

Welcome to Benoni! Hello and welcome, cricket fans around the world. The caravan has rolled into Benoni for the fifth and final T20I of this series between South Africa Women and India Women. The Proteas have already clinched the series with an unassailable 3-1 lead, but make no mistake, the intensity hasn't dropped. For India, this is the final stop on their South African tour and a crucial stepping stone to address their flaws before heading off to face England ahead of the T20 World Cup.
... MATCH DAY ...

Tactical dress rehearsal - The curtain falls on this high-octane five-match T20I series as South Africa Women prepare to host India Women at Willowmoore Park. While the Proteas have already secured the series silverware with a dominant 3-1 lead, the final encounter in Benoni carries significant weight for both camps. For India, it is a vital chance to salvage pride and exit the tour with back-to-back victories following their spirited 14-run win in Johannesburg. Meanwhile, the home side will be eager to prove that their initial three-match winning streak was no fluke and that they can maintain their clinical edge even when tested by a resurgent Indian outfit. India’s batting puzzle and injury alarms - Despite showing flashes of brilliance, India’s star-studded batting lineup is yet to deliver a truly collective performance. Shafali Verma has been the primary aggressor at the top, but the team is searching for that elusive game where the entire top three clicks in unison. Adding to their selection headaches is the fitness of Kranti Gaud, her ankle injury in the previous game, which required a golf cart to exit the field, has left a massive void in the bowling plans. If she is unfit to feature, the pressure will double on the likes of Deepti Sharma, who is fresh off a match-winning five-wicket haul, to lead a reshuffled attack once again against a dangerous South African order. Proteas seek to plug bowling leaks - South Africa may have the trophy in their cabinet, but their recent defensive form remains a major point of concern for the coaching staff. Conceding scores of 192 and 185 in consecutive matches has exposed vulnerabilities in their death-over execution and tactical discipline. While the batting unit showed immense depth in the 4th T20I, recovering well after the early loss of captain Laura Wolvaardt thanks to gritty contributions from Sune Luus and Tazmin Brits, the bowlers must now step up. The Proteas' primary objective will be to tighten the screws during the Powerplay and find a reliable method to suppress India’s middle-order finishers, Richa Ghosh and Harmanpreet Kaur. Form (Last 5 completed T20Is, recent first) - SA - LWWWL | IND - WLLLW. Benoni’s pitch and strategy - Willowmoore Park is renowned for its balanced surface, typically offering a fair contest where neither bat nor ball holds a lopsided advantage. However, given India’s historical struggles with defending totals during this series, the toss will likely dictate the initial momentum, with the chasing side potentially holding a slight psychological edge. With the Women’s T20 World Cup looming in June, this final clash transcends the current scoreline. It serves as a critical laboratory for both teams to refine their Plan B, test bench strength, and finalize the tactical combinations that will serve them on the world stage.
